Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Vertex Capital Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vertex Capital Partners' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Distribution; and Tom Reilly, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by strong market appreciation, robust net inflows, and the successful integration of key acquisitions that expanded our alternatives platform. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Mike. From a financial perspective, Vertex Capital Partners delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $5.3 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the direct impact of AUM expansion on our fee-based revenue model. Our expenses were $3.1 billion, resulting in net income of $1.5 billion. Our expense ratio improved to 38 basis points due to scale advantages and technology-driven efficiencies.

Let me unpack the critical linkage between our assets under management—or AUM—and revenue generation, which remains the lifeblood of our business at Vertex Capital. Our revenue is predominantly fee-based, with about 85% from management fees on average daily AUM, plus performance fees on 15% of strategies, mainly alternatives, and some distribution fees. When AUM grows, revenue follows closely.

Quarter-end AUM hit $1.2 trillion, up 14% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter, pushing average AUM to $1.18 trillion. At a blended 42 basis points fee rate—stable amid compression—this generated $5.1 billion in fee-related revenue, up 14% year-to-date. Performance fees added $320 million, boosted by alpha in long-short equity and private credit.

Breaking down AUM drivers: markets added $62 billion, with equities up 8.1% capturing S&P 500 gains from AI and earnings resilience; fixed income contributed modestly at 1.2%; alternatives lagged slightly on marks. Net flows were $45 billion year-to-date, with ETFs leading at $22 billion, ESG suites strong, and institutional inflows from Middle East SWFs into infrastructure debt.

Every $100 billion AUM change at 42 bps yields about $420 million annualized revenue; Q3's growth added roughly $190 million sequentially, with EBITDA margins expanding to 52% via platform automation.

Before questions, a detailed update on our capital allocation strategy, a cornerstone for superior shareholder returns. With $1.2 trillion AUM up 14% YoY on $45 billion net inflows, we generated $320 million free cash flow, strengthening our balance sheet to $2.8 billion cash and 0.8x net debt-to-EBITDA.

Our framework targets 15% ROIC, achieving 18.2% YTD across three pillars: organic growth (40% of capital, $450 million YTD), scaling high-margin ETFs like our Vertex Smart Beta Equity ETF (VSBX) with $2.5 billion AUM since July, outpacing peers; $100 million in AI quant tools improved efficiency 25%; APAC push with $80 million for Japan/Australia partnerships amid BOJ shifts; EMEA ESG UCITS grew 12% organically.

Inorganic via M&A (25%, $280 million YTD): closed $1.2 billion Pinnacle Alternatives acquisition adding $180 billion private markets AUM, lifting alternatives to 28%; accretive 15% EPS, with $500 million dry powder for digital assets, passing on overvalued deals. Tech/ops resilience (20%, $220 million): $120 million cloud data lakes cut model drift 40%; $60 million cybersecurity for T+1.

Shareholder returns (15%, $170 million): repurchased 2.1 million shares at $145 average, 22% TSR YTD beating KBW by 800 bps; $1.20 dividend at 35% payout.

This balances 12-15% AUM CAGR, 42% margins by 2026.

On M&A, a key inorganic pillar amid fee compression—active equity down 20 bps per Morningstar—and demand for alts/ESG. Q3 closed $1.2 billion Horizon Alternatives, adding $28 billion high-fee (85 bps) private credit, boosting FUM to $1.47 trillion; $150 million synergies by 2025 via cross-selling.

Integration: 95% portfolios on our platform, costs down 18%; 98% retention. Launched co-mingled funds with $800 million inflows. Tuck-in: €450 million EuroQuant, €12 billion quant ETFs, outperforming STOXX by 250 bps; €40 million synergies.

Pipeline: $3 billion in sustainable infra, EM fixed income, APAC JV. Inorganic drove 22% YTD FUM growth.

Efficiency ratios remain core to positioning. Full-year expense ratio at 38 bps, down 12% YoY from 43 bps, below 45 bps peer median. Q3 at 37 bps, best ever; operating margin 42%, up from 38%.

Scale from $85 billion inflows diluted fixed costs; comp up 4% on 12% headcount despite growth. Americas 35 bps on ETF gains; EMEA 42 bps but feeders cut 3 bps; APAC 36 bps via localization.

Passive/ETFs (65% AUM) at 12 bps vs. active 68 bps. Efficiency 2.0: $250 million invested; cloud migration cut middle-office 22%; AI surveillance 35% fewer hours; outsourcing saved $120 million.

Guide 36 bps 2024 on 12-15% AUM growth.

AUM/flow guidance: Q3 AUM $1.25 trillion proxy, up 8% QoQ/15% YoY. Net LT flows $28 billion, YTD $72 billion: equities $18 billion (PINSPX $12 billion); FI $12 billion; alts modest outflow offset by PE feeders. Markets +$35 billion.

Regions: NA 65%, EMEA UCITS, APAC ESG bonds. Tech: AI portal +25% retention.

Q3 guide: $25-30 billion flows; FY $1.35-1.40 trillion on $110-120 billion flows. 2024: $150 billion flows, $1.6 trillion AUM, 12-15% CAGR.

David Patel: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing quant overlays and selective sector bets amid volatility from rates and geopolitics. We launched the Vertex Smart Beta Equity ETF (VSBX) this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $2.5 billion AUM and flows outpacing peers by 20%.

Diving into performance fees and vs. benchmarks: Q3 realized $152 million, +28% QoQ/+22% YoY; FY $478 million beating $420 million guide. Equities (55% AUM): Core Composite 12.8% net vs. S&P 500 11.7% (+110 bps); TTM 28.4% vs. 24.1% (+430 bps). Quant Alpha 15.2% (+360 bps), Sharpe 1.85. EAFE +11.1% vs. MSCI 8.2%; APAC slight lag pivoted to India.

FI (25%): Total Return 6.1% vs. Agg 5.4% (+70 bps); YTD 8.7% vs. 5.9%. Alts: $42 million fees, Opportunities Fund 9.2% vs. Cambridge 7.8%.

Fees now 18% revenue mix. AI risk platform cut drawdowns 15%; launching AI Equity ETF, Climate Credit.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by 30% YoY AUM growth in fixed-income SMAs targeting the $5 trillion wealth transfer, plus partnerships in Japan and Australia yielding $8 billion regional flows.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on cloud-native data lakes, machine learning for risk analytics reducing model drift by 40%, and cybersecurity/regtech for T+1 and crypto rules, alongside outsourcing non-core functions saving $120 million annually.

Mike Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes maintaining disciplined M&A with $500 million dry powder, launching 15 new products in H2 like tokenized PE, and targeting mid-teens organic growth via AI flow predictors and ESG feeders.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your capital allocation strategy and how it's evolving post-acquisitions?

Mike Thompson: Thanks, John. Sarah, would you take that?

Sarah Chen: Happy to, Mike. Our framework remains disciplined around 15% ROIC, with 40% to organic like VSBX and AI tools; 25% M&A like Pinnacle accretive at 15% EPS; 20% tech cutting drift 40%; 15% buybacks at 22% TSR. Post-deals, we're prioritizing sustainable infra with $500 million dry powder, balancing growth and returns amid volatility.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on the impact of recent AUM changes on revenue trajectory?

Sarah Chen: Absolutely. Q3's $45 billion net growth at 42 bps added $190 million revenue; scale lifted margins to 52%. With Q3 flows guide $25-30 billion, expect 10-12% revenue growth FY24, countering compression via alts and tech.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the VSBX fund?

David Patel: Thanks, Emily. VSBX leverages our alpha models with AI optimization, gathering $2.5 billion AUM since July, 20% ahead of peers like QQQT. Q3 net 15.2% vs. S&P 11.7% +360 bps in quant sleeve, Sharpe 1.85 top-quartile.

Emily Chen: And how is the new product VSBX performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Wong: Early flows exceeded targets at $2.5 billion, driven by retail via Schwab/Fidelity and institutional smart-beta demand. APAC partnerships added momentum, aligning with our 5-7% organic guide.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan.

Robert Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Tom Reilly: Sure, Robert. Efficiency 2.0 delivered: cloud migration automated 70% reconciliation, cutting middle-office 22% or 1.5 bps AUM; AI handled 40% surveillance, 35% fewer hours; outsourcing 25% functions saved $120 million at 99.5% uptime. Expense ratio to 36 bps 2024, every bp adds $120 million FCF.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Vertex Capital Partners. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
